summary: Temporary bridge account for cross-team handover + coordinated device collection scheduling
description:
Issue summary:
A departing engineer (name redacted for privacy) requires a short-lived 'bridge' service account to facilitate handover to two teams (Platform & Data). HR has requested a single-window coordinated device collection to occur during the handover week. Support must: 1) provision scoped bridge account with expiration and MFA enforcement, 2) schedule and confirm physical device pickup with Ops, 3) ensure KMS/service-account key handoff is recorded, and 4) confirm all remaining cloud console sessions are revoked.

Impact:
- Potential data exposure if bridge account scope is too broad.
- Delays to project shipments if devices/key handoffs are not completed on schedule.
- HR requires confirmation to complete final payroll/exit workflow.

Environment:
- Internal: corporate G Suite, AWS account redwood-corp-prod, self-service device pickup at SF-office.

Steps / Acceptance criteria:
1) Create bridge account: name format bridge/<firstname>-handoff-YYYYMMDD, expires in 7 days, MFA required, no ability to create new long-lived keys.
2) Grant temporary role: limited to read-only access for the two repos and read-only S3 list on the single bucket containing artifacts.
3) Record KMS key access handoff in the device return ticket and associate the ticket in the asset record in the inventory system.
4) Schedule device pickup with Ops on 2026-03-17 10:00-12:00 PST and confirm courier/desk availability.
5) Revoke all console sessions and rotate any service account keys that were exposed during the handoff window.
6) Attach HR confirmation note and close ticket.

Investigation notes / constraints:
- Engineering manager asked for a 14-day bridge window; security policy prefers <=7 days. We need explicit exception if longer.
- Inventory shows two devices (MacBook Pro 16 2021, serial XZY123; NVIDIA dev-jetson test device). Both flagged BYOD? Inventory notes ambiguous; Ops must verify model and serial at pickup.
- KMS ownership: project-kms-prod is owned by infra-team; on-call requested to be paged for manual key audit during handoff.

Risk mitigations proposed:
- Time-box the bridge account to 7 days automatically via IAM TTL and require a documented escalation procedure to extend.
- Make the bridge account ephemeral (no password; only key-based API tokens created and logged) and require a second approver (Security lead) for any key-creation operations.
- Use a dedicated asset-return form to capture serial numbers and device condition; Ops to upload photos into the inventory record.
